title: Point dualizing identification is compatible with coefficient change
statement:
Use the Poincare duality conventions [def-pod-conventions] at a coefficient stage $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$, and put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $C\in D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$, with constructibility and finite Tor amplitude as in [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Put $F_\Lambda=\operatorname{Fib}_s$ [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], $c=F_\Lambda C$, $D_sC=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\omega_{s,\Lambda})$ [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and let
$$j_{\Lambda,C}:F_\Lambda(D_sC)\xrightarrow{\sim}c^\vee$$
be the specified identification of [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex], where $c^\vee=R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(c,\Lambda)$. Let $Q$ be finite reduction $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ ($1\leq m\leq n$), integral reduction $\mathcal O_E\to A_{E,n}$, integral scalar extension for a finite coefficient-field extension, rationalization, or extension at a common finite field stage. On point sheaves use the stipulated coefficient functor $Q_s$ and on coefficient modules use $q$. Write
$$t_{Q,B}:q(F_\Lambda B)\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{\Lambda'}(Q_sB)$$
for the canonical sections/coefficient comparison, natural in $B\in D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$: for $\mathcal O_E\to A_{E,n}$ it is the sections/derived-reduction isomorphism of [lem-pod-point-sections-derived-reduction]; for integral scalar extension and for extension at a common finite field stage it is the inverse of the sections scalar-extension isomorphism $\varphi$ of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] (rationalized in the latter case); for rationalization it is the identity, $F_E$ being $\Gamma(s,-)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E$ by [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]; for $A_{E,n}\to A_{E,m}$ it is the map $\Gamma(s,B)\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m}\to\Gamma(s,B\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}A_{E,m})$ induced by tensoring sections, whose invertibility on $D^b_{ctf}(s,A_{E,n})$ is part of the present assertion. Its compatibility with the unit and tensor constraints is that of [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor]. Let $\delta_{Q,C}:Q_s(D_sC)\to D_s(Q_sC)$ be the canonical internal-Hom comparison using the identity-adjunction coefficient comparison $Q_s\omega_{s,\Lambda}\cong\omega_{s,\Lambda'}$, and let $b_{Q,c}:q(c^\vee)\to(qc)^\vee$ be the canonical derived module-dual comparison. The site comparisons are those of [lem-fix-operation-reduction] on its domains and the finite-Tor comparisons of [thm-sf-ctf-stability]. Then
$$t_{Q,C}^{\vee}\circ j_{\Lambda',Q_sC}\circ F_{\Lambda'}(\delta_{Q,C})\circ t_{Q,D_sC}
=b_{Q,c}\circ q(j_{\Lambda,C}).$$
Both sides are morphisms from $q(F_\Lambda D_sC)$ to $(qc)^\vee$; $t_{Q,C}^{\vee}$ is precomposition by $t_{Q,C}$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pod-point-dual-coefficient-domains] to the stated $C$ and $Q$. It gives the specified natural isomorphisms $t_{Q,C}$ and $t_{Q,D_sC}$, including the finite-quotient map, and places $D_sC$, $Q_sC$ and $D_s(Q_sC)$ in the required finite-Tor domains. This also fixes the normalization of $\delta_{Q,C}$.

Put $d=F_\Lambda D_sC$ and $e=e_{\Lambda,C}:d\otimes^Lc\to\Lambda$. By [lem-pod-point-dual-evaluation-transport], $\operatorname{ev}_c\circ(j_{\Lambda,C}\otimes1)=e$, with the corresponding target identity. Its coefficient-pairing equality says
$$e'\circ((F_{\Lambda'}\delta_{Q,C}\circ t_{Q,D_sC})\otimes t_{Q,C})=E,\qquad E=q(e)\circ\nu_q,$$
where $e'=e_{\Lambda',Q_sC}$ and $\nu_q:qd\otimes^Lqc\to q(d\otimes^Lc)$ is the coefficient tensor constraint.

Let $L$ be the asserted left composite. Uncurrying by [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws] gives
$$\operatorname{ev}_{c'}\circ((j_{\Lambda',Q_sC}\circ F_{\Lambda'}\delta_{Q,C}\circ t_{Q,D_sC})\otimes t_{Q,C}),\quad c'=F_{\Lambda'}Q_sC.$$
The target evaluation identity in step 2 turns this into its pairing equality, so this transpose is $E$. For $R=b_{Q,c}\circ q(j_{\Lambda,C})$, the definition of $b$ as the transpose of scalar-changed module evaluation gives
$$\operatorname{ev}_{qc}\circ(b_{Q,c}\otimes1)=q(\operatorname{ev}_c)\circ\nu_{q,c^\vee,c}.$$
Naturality of the coefficient tensor constraint makes the transpose of $R$ equal to
$$q(\operatorname{ev}_c\circ(j_{\Lambda,C}\otimes1))\circ\nu_q=q(e)\circ\nu_q=E.$$
The tensor--Hom adjunction is a bijection, so equal transposes imply $L=R$. No invertibility of $\delta$ or $b$ is needed. At $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ this calculation is performed at a common finite field stage and represents equality in its finite-stage category [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point].
